title: NOSDCP taught under the Ministry of Earth Sciences with the Coast Guard as 'nodal agency'; the P&I club taught as liable for all costs; DPA/DGS placed in front of the statutory pollution report
authority: PRIMARY. (1) Government of India (Allocation of Business) Rules, 1961, as amended upto Amendment Series no. 386 dated 22 July 2026 (Cabinet Secretariat), Ministry of Defence, Department of Defence, item 17 - 'All matters relating to Coast Guard Organisation, including-' (b) combating oil spills in maritime zones except in the waters of ports and within 500 metres of offshore platforms, coastal refineries and associated facilities; (c) 'Central Coordinating Agency for Combating of Oil Pollution in the coastal and marine environment of various maritime zones'; (d) 'implementation of National Contingency Plan for oil spill disaster'. Registry SRC-INDIA-AOB-RULES-2026. (2) Indian Coast Guard, Marine Environment page (read 16 Sep 2026): nominated in 1986 as the Central Coordinating Authority; NOSDCP approved 1993; ports within port limits, oil-handling agencies up to 500 m, coastal States/UTs shoreline; revised edition-2015 released 9 Apr 2015. SRC-ICG-MARINE-ENVIRONMENT-2026. (3) Chairman NOSDCP circulars (compilation 'NOSDCP Circular 01 - 2025'): Coast Guard 'designated as the Central Coordinating Authority'; the Business Rules wording 'Central Coordinating Agency' also quoted; Amendments No. 2 and 3 to the 2015 edition; MoES/NIO a section heading among agencies with responsibilities. SRC-ICG-NOSDCP-CIRCULARS-2025. (4) ICG OSD Policy 2025: 'Central Coordinating Authority (CCA)'; Tier-1 responsibility by area. SRC-ICG-OSD-POLICY-2025. (5) INCOIS OOSA: autonomous body under MoES providing oil-spill trajectory prediction - the genuine MoES link. SRC-INCOIS-OOSA-2026.
rationale: The ministry error is a false regulatory proposition on the reported card and is corrected everywhere it occurs, which is only QB1_A Q15 and its SQ twin: a repo-wide search for Earth Sciences / MoES found one other use (QB9_E, marine spatial planning), which is correct and untouched. The same review of the whole card found two further propositions wrong on both QB1_A Q15 and Q14 - the P&I club as the liable party for all costs, and the DPA/DGS fixed reporting chain - and the Founder authorised correcting Q14's three limbs in the same event so the two cards agree. Terminology follows the two primary voices exactly: Coast Guard material says Central Coordinating Authority, the Business Rules say Central Coordinating Agency; the cards teach the first and record the second, and do not merge them.
note: SCOPE. Two cards on one page (QB1_A Q14, Q15) and their SQ free-sample twins; governed changelog entry and its derived index; known_traps entry 133; five source-registry rows; one content gate pair registered in the release runner. NOT DONE, deliberately, per the approval: QB9_A Q8 and oralnotes/simon-notes-p3.html tier tonnage limits (Follow-up A) and simon-notes-p3's OPRC 1993 date (Follow-up B) - both logged in entry 133, neither corrected; Bunkers Convention status for India not reviewed; QB1_A Q14's PANS 96-hour line not reviewed. The applier derives from the baseline commit, not the working tree, so a re-run reproduces the authorised bytes. REVIEW AMENDMENT (17 Sep 2026): an independent pre-release review accepted the correction and required four wording changes, applied in bc2a646 - (1) direct action 'where the applicable liability convention provides', CLC 1992 as the example, Bunkers Convention not named on this India card; (2) no unqualified 'the Coast Guard leads the response' - responsibility by location; (3) Q14 scenario escalates to Tier 2/3 under NOSDCP with the Coast Guard in the coordinating/overall response role, not 'ICG declares'; (4) Q15 60-second answer cut to 102 words. The same review supplied a lead to the NOSDCP 2015 plan text for the queued tier-tonnage audit; it is not relied on here.

cards.rationale: The card the candidate reported ('NOSDCP - Explain.'). Ministry of Earth Sciences named as the authority at four sites (body, 15-second answer, reg-box, numbers box) and the Coast Guard called 'nodal (implementing) agency' at three. Rebuilt answer region: Ministry of Defence; Indian Coast Guard as Central Coordinating Authority with the Allocation of Business Rules' 'Central Coordinating Agency' kept distinct; DG ICG as Chairman NOSDCP; who responds where (maritime zones / port limits / 500 m / shoreline); tiers without tonnage; liability restated (shipowner liable, normally within convention limits, P&I as insurer, CLC/Fund vs bunker regime); reporting under MARPOL Protocol I with the Company/DPA in parallel; DGS Circulars reg-item replaced. Question text unchanged. Stamped v1.1. Amended in bc2a646 after independent review, before release: direct action stated jurisdiction-neutrally (no Bunkers Convention named); response responsibility stated by location; Tier 2/3 as escalation, not a declaration rule; 60-second answer shortened.

Same facts wrong on the adjacent OPRC card, authorised for inclusion: 'nodal agency' (60-second answer), the P&I club 'strictly liable for ALL costs' (body, 60-second answer, CE tip, scenario anchor, memory map) and the fixed chain 'CE -> Master -> DPA -> ICG/Coast Guard -> DGS -> port authority' (body, CE tip), plus 'DGS' in the examiner trap. Limited to those three limbs; the unsourced PANS 96-hour line in the numbers box is deliberately untouched. Question text unchanged. Stamped v1.1. Amended in bc2a646 after independent review, before release: direct action stated jurisdiction-neutrally; 15-second answer and Polluter Pays line no longer imply the Coast Guard always leads; scenario anchor escalates to Tier 2/3 instead of 'ICG declares'.
